hints.content: The graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$ can be transformed to get the graph of $y=\sqrt{x+1}$.  [[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
Suppose $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ and $g(x)=\sqrt{x+1}$.  

>$\begin{align}f(x)&=\sqrt{x}\\\\
f(x+1)&=\sqrt{x+1}\\\\
\end{align}$

Notice that what is on the right-hand side of the equal sign is $g(x)$.  Therefore, $g(x)=f(x+1)$.  

Since function $g$ can be built from function $f$, the graph of function $g$ is a transformation of the graph of function $f$.

hints.content:
- Replacing $x$ with $x+1$ shifts the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$ to the left by $1$ unit.


Therefore, *the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$ is obtained by shifting the graph of $y=\sqrt{x+1}$ to the left by $\text{ }1$ unit.*

**The graph that corresponds with this transformation is graph $B$:**

>[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A square root graph is on an x y coordinate plane. The x- and y- axes scale by one. The graph has an endpoint at (negative one, zero) passing through (zero, one) and (three, two).
